name: Jane App vs Valant
title: Jane App vs Valant: Practice Management Comparison for Mental Health
description: Compare Jane App and Valant EHR for behavioral health practices. See differences in pricing, e-prescribing, outcome tracking, and practice management features.

summary.bottom_line: Jane App is a multi-disciplinary platform with strong telehealth and Canadian roots, while Valant is a psychiatrist-designed behavioral health EHR with e-prescribing and outcome tracking. Choose Jane App for multi-disciplinary practices or therapists; choose Valant for psychiatric practices needing e-prescribing with EPCS.

sections.heading: Jane App vs Valant: Overview
sections.content: Jane App and Valant serve overlapping but distinct markets. Jane App is a Canadian-built multi-disciplinary platform serving physiotherapy, chiropractic, massage, and mental health practices with strong telehealth and AI features. Valant was founded by a psychiatrist and is purpose-built for behavioral health with features psychiatrists need: e-prescribing with EPCS for controlled substances, PDMP integration, and built-in outcome measurement. Valant is better suited for psychiatric practices while Jane App is more versatile for non-prescribing mental health providers.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Jane App has transparent public pricing starting at $54/month (Balance) up to $99/month (Thrive). Valant uses quote-based pricing typically ranging from $100-300 per provider per month depending on practice size and features. Valant does not offer a free trial while Jane App offers 14 days. Jane App is generally more affordable and accessible for smaller practices, while Valant's pricing reflects its specialized psychiatric features.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: The critical difference is e-prescribing: Valant offers full e-prescribing with EPCS (Electronic Prescribing for Controlled Substances) and PDMP integration—essential for psychiatrists. Jane App does not offer e-prescribing. Valant also has built-in outcome tracking with PHQ-9, GAD-7, and other standardized assessments. Jane App's strengths are its AI Scribe for documentation, strong telehealth, mobile app, and multi-disciplinary flexibility. Jane App has a mobile app; Valant does not.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: The choice largely depends on whether you prescribe medications:

recommendations.when: You're a non-prescribing therapist or counselor, run a multi-disciplinary practice, want transparent pricing, or prefer mobile app access
You're a psychiatrist or psychiatric NP needing e-prescribing with EPCS, want built-in outcome measurement, or run IOP/PHP programs
You have a mixed practice with both prescribers (Valant) and therapists (possibly Jane App)—though using two systems adds complexity

faqs.q: Does Jane App have e-prescribing like Valant?
faqs.a: No, Jane App does not offer e-prescribing. Valant includes full e-prescribing with EPCS for controlled substances and PDMP integration. If you prescribe medications, especially controlled substances, Valant is the better choice.

faqs.q: Is Valant good for therapists who don't prescribe?
faqs.a: Valant can work for non-prescribing therapists, but it's designed primarily for psychiatrists and may be overkill (and more expensive) for therapy-only practices. Jane App or SimplePractice may be more cost-effective for therapists.
Valant has more robust built-in outcome tracking with PHQ-9, GAD-7, and other standardized assessments integrated into clinical workflows. Jane App has limited outcome tracking capabilities.

faqs.q: Does Valant have a mobile app?
faqs.a: No, Valant does not have a mobile app. Jane App offers mobile apps for both iOS and Android. If mobile access is important, Jane App has the advantage.
